title: Make constraint waivers portable / version-controllable
description:
Waivers created via `sutra_constraints action=waive` are stored in the local workspace db (under `.sutra/<workspace>/`, which is gitignored) rather than in the tracked `.sutra/rules.toml`. Consequences: they don't travel via git, so a fresh clone, CI, or a teammate loses every waiver and its rationale — and the review report re-flags everything that was deliberately accepted. The rationale text (often the most valuable "why this clone/unsafe/allow is fine" knowledge) is stranded on one machine.

Surfaced during chitta sutra-adoption: we created 23 waivers (2 #[allow] + 21 no-clone-driven-dev groups), all now local-only.

Design question (why this is HITL): where should the source of truth live?
- (a) Keep the db authoritative, add an export/import (waivers → a tracked file, e.g. `.sutra/waivers.toml`, synced on waive/unwaive).
- (b) Make a tracked file authoritative and load waivers from it at parse time (like rules.toml constraints), db becomes a cache.
- (c) A `[[waiver]]` block inside rules.toml itself, keyed by constraint_id + file + symbol + rationale.

Consider stability of the key across reparses (line numbers shift; symbol_qualified_name is more stable) and how introduced-only semantics interact with a tracked waiver list.

decisions.decision: File-authoritative (.sutra/accepted.toml), DB tables demoted to a freshness-gated projection
decisions.rationale: One writer direction (file->DB) makes bidirectional drift impossible; merges happen in human-readable git-mergeable TOML; git blame is the audit trail. The cache preserves the existing SQLite read paths (guard find_waiver, report partition, evaluate_dd ack subtraction) unchanged behind an mtime/hash freshness gate, so guard and report keep deriving acceptance through the SAME table (guard must predict the audit, lesson 019f9add). Covers BOTH sutra/305 report-only instance acks and the original guard-honored waivers without re-coupling the two 305 deliberately split.
decisions.rejected_alternative: (a) DB-authoritative + export/import — bidirectional sync drifts and conflicts across branches. (c) inline [[waiver]]/[[ack]] in rules.toml — buries authored rules under a 95-entry instance ledger and routes every ack through the ratchet guard. Also rejected 'no cache, both surfaces parse the file directly' — forks/rewrites two read paths and re-parses TOML on every edit.

decisions.decision: Key file entries by constraint NAME, not the blake3 id; enforce unique constraint names at rule-parse time
decisions.rationale: id = blake3(kind,params,scope), so a scope/param edit reshapes it and orphans every entry keyed to it — in a tracked file that means a confusing diff and lost rationale team-wide. Names survive such edits and read cleanly in review. Enforcing uniqueness at parse time (rules.rs) makes name a safe key; verified current rules.toml has 34/34 named, 0 duplicates, so no existing repo breaks. resolve_ref still surfaces Unknown/Ambiguous as warnings (never a silent drop) for robustness.
decisions.rejected_alternative: id-with-name-fallback: fragile (orphans on rule edits) and unreadable in diffs. Uniqueness-as-resolve-time-warning-only: weaker; a dup name would silently pick one constraint.

decisions.decision: No timestamps in the tracked file; count as u32 in schema
decisions.rationale: created_at/updated_at in a tracked file only produce merge churn; verified nothing reads them semantically (only ORDER BY created_at DESC for display, preserved by projecting in canonical file order). count as u32 makes a negative accepted-count unrepresentable, converted to i64 at the DB boundary.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Carry timestamps for parity with the DB rows — rejected: merge churn with zero semantic consumer.

implementation_plan:
Types-first skeleton approved (src/constraints/accepted.rs, type-checks). Decisions settled + verified (see decisions field). Implementation units, compiler-driven bottom-up, commit per verified unit:

**A. rules.rs name uniqueness** — in Rules::all_constraints, after building `out`, count Constraint.name occurrences; emit a ConstraintParseError per duplicated name (same channel as other rule errors). Verified: current rules.toml 34/34 named, 0 dups. Test in rules.rs #[cfg(test)].

**B. Migration 0058_accepted_sync_marker** — add a sync-marker column/row so the freshness gate can detect file changes. Options: extend index_meta with `accepted_file_hash TEXT` (id=1 row) OR a tiny kv. Prefer index_meta column (single-row, already the generation home). Register in migrations.rs after 0057.

**C. DB CRUD (db/constraints.rs + db/mod.rs)** — `delete_all_constraint_waivers`, `delete_all_constraint_instance_acks` (truncate for reproject); `get_accepted_sync_marker`/`set_accepted_sync_marker` (index_meta). Reuse existing create_* CRUD for insert.

**D. accepted.rs bodies** — load_accepted_file (fail-loud IO/parse), write_accepted_file (canonical sort: constraint,file,symbol,snippet), resolve_ref (unique-name lookup), resolve_accepted (partition -> ResolvedWaiver/Ack + warnings), ensure_cache_fresh (hash accepted.toml; if != marker, truncate+reinsert both tables in one txn, update marker, return warnings), upsert/remove mutations (file-first, canonical write), migrate_db_to_file (one-time DB->file when file absent).

**E. Cross-process freshness wiring** — report/orient/violations run server-side (writable Db): call ensure_cache_fresh at head, surface warnings. GUARD (read-only conn, latency-critical): stat accepted.toml vs marker; if stale, resolve waivers in-memory from the file (reuse resolve_accepted) WITHOUT persisting — same data the reproject would produce, no divergence, no write from the hot path (lessons 019f9add same-derivation, 019f8a98 hot-path handle). If fresh, read cache as today.

**F. MCP actions (tools/constraints.rs)** — waive/unwaive -> upsert_waiver/remove_waiver + reproject; ack/baseline/unack -> upsert_ack/remove_ack + reproject. violations/list surface AcceptedWarning (unknown/ambiguous constraint refs). Call migrate_db_to_file once on first touch.

**G. .gitignore** — add `!.sutra/accepted.toml` to the tracked allowlist (alongside rules.toml/owners.toml).

**Tests**: rules dup-name (A); db truncate + marker CRUD (C); accepted roundtrip/resolve/warnings + freshness reproject (D); guard stale-file in-memory resolution == cache result (E); MCP file-first + warning surfacing (F).
execution_record:
Types-first gate complete + foundation landed & tested; end-to-end integration (Units E+F) deliberately deferred to a focused follow-up (sutra/308) because it is coupled and lands on contract-sensitive files.

LANDED (committed, verified):
- 877b5ec Unit A: parse-time duplicate constraint-name rejection (names are the portable key). 2 tests; verified rules.toml has 34/34 named, 0 dups.
- 7a5059e Units B/C/D/G: migration 0059 accepted_sync marker; db reproject_accepted (transactional truncate+reinsert+stamp) + get_accepted_sync_marker + Waiver/AckProjection; src/constraints/accepted.rs (file schema name-keyed no-timestamps, resolve_ref Unknown/Ambiguous-as-warnings, ensure_cache_fresh server gate, resolve_waivers_for_guard read-only path, file-first mutations, migrate_db_to_file); .gitignore allowlist. 9 accepted-module tests. Full suite 823 lib + 61 db + 66 constraints green, clippy clean in new files.

PENDING (sutra/308, Units E+F — coupled, must land together):
- E: gate the report path at evaluate_dd head (single chokepoint for review.rs:362 / orient.rs:365 / constraints.rs:222) with migrate_db_to_file THEN ensure_cache_fresh; guard read-only path (evaluate_raw ~642) uses resolve_waivers_for_guard on stale; orient.rs:350/354 + constraints.rs:84/367 direct display reads also need the gate.
- F: rewire handle_waive->upsert_waiver, handle_ack/handle_baseline->upsert_ack, each followed by reproject; switch handle_unwaive/handle_unack from waiver_id/ack_id to KEY-based (projection re-mints row ids each reproject, so ids are unstable); update the 305 DB-id-based tests.

HAZARDS for 308 (discovered during this session):
1. E-without-F truncates freshly-written DB waivers (report reprojects from a file that lacks them) — land coupled.
2. Empty/absent accepted.toml reprojects to EMPTY -> wipes pre-existing DB waivers. Order MUST be migrate(seed once, file-existence-gated) then ensure. Add regression test: DB waivers + no file -> nothing lost after first review.
3. AcceptedWarning surfacing: CheckOutcome has no warnings channel; decide log-only vs. structured report field (relates to sutra/306 acked-instance surfacing).

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Review: approve with notes. Core design (file-authoritative, name-keyed, DB as projection) is sound with strong hazard test coverage. Three medium findings for follow-up: (1) waiving a nameless constraint silently produces an inert entry, (2) write_accepted_file is non-atomic (O_TRUNC + write, no temp+rename), (3) no file-level lock on read-modify-write mutations. All bounded in current usage.
